newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SCHULTZ STRIKES BUT AUSTRALIA MAKE SOUND START.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SCHULTZ STRIKES BUT AUSTRALIA MAKE SOUND START.

text.p: Fast bowler Brett Schultz quickly made his mark on his recall to the South African team but it was the Australians who had the better of the first morning of the third and final cricket test match at Centurion Park on Friday.

South African captain Hansie Cronje won the toss but his gamble of putting the tourists in to bat failed to pay significant dividends as Australia reached 64 for the loss of just two wickets by lunch.
Schultz, however, who replaced the injured Shaun Pollock, did produce an early breakthrough when, in his fourth over, he bowled Matthew Hayden through the gate for 10.

It was welcome relief for the left-arm fast bowler who played his last test at the same venue over a year ago against England. He incurred the wrath of the selectors when he went into that test with a buttock strain and was unable to make any significant contribution.
Schultz was also involved in the second wicket when he punished Matthew Elliott's injudicious hook at an Allan Donald bouncer by taking a fine running catch on the fine-leg boundary. Elliott made 10.
Second test hero Mark Waugh arrived at the crease just before lunch while Australian skipper Mark Taylor survived the session in his personal battle for batting form to reach 22 not out.
It ended a run of nine test innings in which the beleaguered Taylor had failed to reach 20.

South Africa made two other changes to the side which lost the second test and the series in Port Elizabeth, with Herschelle Gibbs and Paul Adams being replaced by all-rounder Lance Klusener and off-spinner Pat Symcox.
